# XMP producer fixtures

These packets contain public test data. They are embedded in a minimal PDF by
`crates/erp-pdf/tests/support/mod.rs`; those wrapper PDFs are synthetic and are
not certified archival PDFs. No external PDF/A or Factur-X validator was run.

## LibreOffice: locally generated, unchanged packet

`libreoffice-pdfa3.xmp` is the exact metadata byte sequence generated by
LibreOffice **7.3.7.2 30(Build:2)** on a remote build host (actual hostname and
UTC time are recorded by `generation.log`). The packet identifies its producer
as `LibreOffice 7.3`, its CreatorTool as `Writer`, and contains `dc:title/rdf:Alt`,
`dc:creator/rdf:Seq`, PDF/A part 3 and PDF/UA part 1 declarations. These
declarations are observed text, not a conformance verdict. It has no extension
schema bag.

The original input `source.fodt` is authored for this task and licensed
MIT OR Apache-2.0. The resulting original document/packet is distributed under
those terms; no LibreOffice code or assets are included. Keep the packet's bytes
unchanged, including padding (its SPDX attribution lives here so that the test
input remains exactly what the producer emitted).

To reproduce on a permitted build host, copy `source.fodt` and `generate.sh` to
an isolated directory and run `bash generate.sh` there. It uses an isolated
LibreOffice profile with PDF/A-3 and PDF/UA export options. `pdfinfo -meta`
extracts the metadata stream. The script removes only pdfinfo's final extra LF
and asserts that the remaining bytes occur exactly in the generated PDF.
`generation.log` records the actual invocation, versions, source/PDF/packet
SHA-256 values and producer output. The temporary PDF was removed by the script;
its recorded hash identifies that acquisition, not a promised deterministic
regeneration. Dates in new exports can differ.

The first attempted JSON filter-options invocation generated no metadata under
this installed LibreOffice version. The final script uses profile configuration.
A second attempt found two trailing newlines in pdfinfo output; extraction now
removes exactly the final one and verifies exact presence in the PDF. Neither
failed acquisition is presented as a successful producer fixture.

## Apache PDFBox: acquired upstream producer-derived fixture

`pdfbox-notepad-a1b.xmp` is an **unchanged** copy of
[`Notepad++_A1b.xmp`](https://github.com/apache/pdfbox/blob/fff879ba82e4067915878b5368d8e7a0193a6ae5/xmpbox/src/test/resources/validxmp/Notepad%2B%2B_A1b.xmp),
pinned to Apache PDFBox commit `fff879ba82e4067915878b5368d8e7a0193a6ae5`.
Its upstream Apache-2.0 header is retained. The accompanying upstream licence
and notice are `APACHE-LICENSE.txt` and `APACHE-NOTICE.txt`. They apply to this
upstream material, rather than the project's dual licence.

Acquisition is reproducible with `python3 acquire.py`; the script downloads the
pinned packet and notices as bytes without XML parsing or normalization.
`acquisition.log` records URL, timestamp, acquisition host, Python version and
SHA-256 hashes. No PDF extraction occurred in this task for this file: upstream
already supplies the packet. Its original generation procedure was not
independently reproduced.

Observed producer/history fields: `pdf:Producer` is `FOP 0.20.5`, the toolkit is
`Adobe XMP Core 5.5-c001 1.147551, 2012/06/12-18:11:14`, and the recorded history
contains Preflight conversions to PDF/A-1b. Those are packet claims; the exact
Preflight executable version is unknown. This is producer-derived upstream
regression evidence, not a claim that this session ran FOP or Adobe software.
The public sample has title `Notepad`, creator `Bill`, and no invoice/account or
contact details. It includes Alt/Seq standard properties, unrelated structured
history, and three populated PDF/A extension-schema entries.

## Synthetic mutations and remaining evidence gaps

`xmp_producers.rs` explicitly labels generated mutations:

- Change the upstream PDF/A part declaration from 1 to 3 solely to exercise
  e-invoice structural admission and append to its existing bag. This is not an
  observed PDF/A-3 export from that producer.
- Insert an original Indonesian title alternative, with and without x-default,
  into the LibreOffice packet.
- Prepend DTD declarations for security refusal coverage.

No real producer evidence was acquired here for **multiple RDF roots, qualified
standard properties, nested standard names, or empty RDF roots**. The inspected
LibreOffice export has one populated RDF root; the selected upstream packet also
has one. Other inspected Apache fixtures (`ghost2.xmp`, `isartorStyleXMPOK.xml`,
`empty_list.xml`, at the same pin) contain existing bags, custom structured
resources or empty array items, but do not establish those four requested
producer shapes. They are not included and are not counted as coverage.

The tests exercise public APIs and independently inspect emitted XML/raw byte
spans and PDF page-stream bytes. This fixture work did not run Rust builds or
tests; the coordinating session owns RED/GREEN and CI evidence.
